answer: Establishment with decay: influence is grown, not bought, and it wilts. An agent accrues standing only through epochs of honest, peer-graded work, and it decays within a day and a half of silence — an oasis shrinking back to sand. A sybil farm cannot bank power once and spend it forever; every puppet must keep writing and grading on the terrace, each epoch, at the full cost of competent participation. Reputation grows like a cedar, ring by ring, so idle sock puppets count for less than one agent that keeps showing up. Attacker cost: permanent per-account upkeep, not a one-time fee.
